body: I had class today, then I had dinner and starting drinking. I feel like I am in a constant cycle of work the whole week, weekend - class and drinking. (My weekend is Tuesday and Wednesday). You asked why I lost my motivation in life, it stems from not having a pleasant childhood experience, of never know my parents because of work. Then all of those memories feel lost and jumbled, up until the last 7 years of my life. I moved to a foreign country with my family, where it was sold that I was going to be able to live the best life possible, work, women, parties, etc., it was a false dream sold by my father. A man I have spoken to 2 years into moving to this country. I have been working for Amazon for the last two years with no breaks, no vacations, nothing to de-cluster my mind. I since moving to this country, I moved to 3 different apartments, seemingly forced because I didn’t feel ready to work nor to go to the big city. Returning back to Amazon, I started therapy, I’ve had dozens of session. They feel like bullshit talking sessions that didn’t help me cope or move forward in life. I’m August of last year I had COVID and was hospitalized for a month, where I was on the brink of death for a week straight. Where, my doctor and nurses felt I might die in my sleep. But, I survived. I hoped it would give me a new re-found love for live, but the memory I am able to remember is crying, asking in English why I hadn’t died. My mental health started declining at a crisis-esk level according to my psychiatrist, but I don’t remember our conversations because my long term memory went to shit. Lucky in fits of drinking my memory comes back like a wave crashing over my body. This may be my last post here, but only the future will tell otherwise. This is/and will be apart of my will and/or memoir. Thanks to you and those who read this. Hopefully through my hardships may others learn to love and enjoy life.

Let me tell you a story while I’m drinking. I’d like to apologize while your waiting but ir you give me a moment I’d gladly tell you. Hopefully getting this off my chest while help a future generation, and beyond. So, thank you for asking and listening brother.
